intro: Every open question this build ran into, with what we can answer today, what we cannot, and how to close it. Nothing here is resolved by assumption. Where an answer exists, it cites the source. Where it does not, the row says so and names the specific thing that would settle it.

areas.name: Commercial terms
areas.note: What the link actually pays and whether it attributes.

areas.name: Demand
areas.note: Whether anyone is looking for this.

areas.name: Editorial
areas.note: What we can honestly say, and in what voice.

areas.name: Compliance
areas.note: What the program and the regulator require.

areas.name: Technical
areas.note: Whether the site is findable and sound.

areas.name: Brand
areas.note: What this publication is and who it is for.

questions.question: Which exact products do the five submitted links point to?
questions.answer: All five resolved. They are three air fryers and two meat thermometers, with ASINs B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH, B0DHZTCNR5 and B0DZFD6R9Z.
questions.have: Each short link was followed and the landing product page recorded on 2026-11-20.
questions.missing: The intended ASIN for each link, as the requester meant it. None was supplied, so the field stays null.
questions.matters: Everything downstream depends on the ASIN. A wrong ASIN sends a reader to the wrong product.
questions.howToFind: Confirm the five ASINs against the Associates 'Product Links' view, or by eye against the product pages.

questions.question: Is the short code in each link the ASIN?
questions.answer: No. The codes are not ASINs and do not match the destination ASINs.
questions.have: Observed by following each link: the code and the destination ASIN differ in all five cases.
questions.missing: What the short codes actually encode. That is not published.
questions.matters: Anyone treating the code as an ASIN would build broken links.
questions.howToFind: Already settled by observation. No further work needed.

questions.question: Do the five products belong to one niche, or two?
questions.answer: Two, with a shared job: three air fryers and two meat thermometers. The overlap is real — the thermometer listings explicitly name air fryer as a supported use — but they are separate buying decisions.
questions.have: Product categories from the official listings, plus an air-fryer reference on both thermometer listings.
questions.missing: Whether the requester wants one publication covering both, or two focused sites.
questions.matters: Search engines reward topical focus. Two unrelated categories on one small domain dilutes it.
questions.howToFind: Decision, not research: confirm the intended scope. Recommendation is in the suggestions register (SUG-02).
questions.sourceLabel: CHEF iQ listing, references air fryer use

questions.question: Is shopnow047c-20 a live, enrolled Associates tracking ID?
questions.answer: Unconfirmed. It is applied to every outbound link, but confirming enrolment requires the Associates dashboard.
questions.have: The ID itself, supplied by the requester.
questions.missing: Proof it is active, and that it is the ID this site should use.
questions.matters: If it is not enrolled, every click on this site earns nothing and the site is a hobby.
questions.howToFind: Sign in to Associates Central, open Account Settings, confirm the Store/Tracking ID list contains shopnow047c-20. Then click one link and confirm it appears in the tracking report.

questions.question: What commission does each product actually pay?
questions.answer: Not established. Rates vary by category and change; no current public table was verifiable at build time.
questions.have: Categories: air fryers fall under Home & Kitchen; thermometers under Home & Kitchen too.
questions.missing: The current applicable rate, and any fixed-amount bounty for either category.
questions.matters: Without it, no ordering between products is defensible, and no revenue estimate is honest.
questions.howToFind: Associates Central publishes current rates and any bounty offers inside the account. Record the rate with the date it was read.

questions.question: Do the submitted link.amazon short links comply with the Operating Agreement?
questions.answer: Unresolved. Published policy clearly constrains third-party shorteners and requires the destination not be obscured. Whether Amazon's own short domain satisfies that is not stated in the text we could verify.
questions.have: Participation Requirements §6(w) and §6(v), quoted verbatim in the policy register.
questions.missing: An authoritative statement about link.amazon specifically.
questions.matters: If it is non-compliant, a site built on those links is at risk of termination.
questions.howToFind: Ask Associates support directly and keep the written reply. Meanwhile the site does not depend on them — it links to amazon.com product pages.

questions.question: Is anyone searching for these products or these questions?
questions.answer: Unknown. No search volume data exists for this project, and none has been assumed.
questions.have: Five editorial hypotheses for question-shaped guides, written as working titles: the four from the brief plus one thermometer guide.
questions.missing: Any impression, click, or query data. Search Console is not verified and the analytics collector is not deployed.
questions.matters: The brief asks for trending, high-converting topics. Trending is a measurement, not a guess.
questions.howToFind: Verify Search Console, submit the sitemap, and read the Queries report after 2–4 weeks. That replaces instinct with measured demand.

questions.question: Which of the hypothesised guide topics should be written first, and in what order?
questions.answer: Hypothesis only. The capacity checklist is the best starting bet because it applies to all three air fryers and does not depend on any product outperforming another.
questions.have: Five working titles, deliberately not framed as popularity claims.
questions.missing: Evidence of which question people actually arrive with.
questions.matters: Publishing order is the main lever on a new site.
questions.howToFind: Ship all five, then let Search Console query data reorder them. See SUG-05.
questions.sourceLabel: Every guide published on this site

questions.question: Has anyone here used these products?
questions.answer: No. No hands-on testing occurred and no page claims any.
questions.have: Official listing specifications for each product.
questions.missing: Any hands-on experience, or a tester to provide it.
questions.matters: The FTC forbids describing experience you do not have. This single fact caps how confident the writing can honestly be.
questions.howToFind: Either obtain review units and test them, or keep the site permanently in 'how to decide' voice rather than 'we tested' voice. Recommendation: state the policy on the About page and hold it.
questions.sourceLabel: FTC: "You can't talk about your experience with a product you haven't tried."

questions.question: What can be stated as fact about each product?
questions.answer: Only what the official listing states: capacity, form factor, named features, included accessories, material.
questions.have: A per-row status on every specification: verified, claim, unverified, or withheld.
questions.missing: Wattage, dimensions, warranty, and calibration records — none were verifiable from an official source.
questions.matters: A spec table with invented numbers is worse than no table, because it looks authoritative.
questions.howToFind: Manufacturer specification sheets for wattage and dimensions; the warranty document for terms. Add each only with a source link.

questions.question: Can we show prices?
questions.answer: No. Not without API access, and price tracking is prohibited outright.
questions.have: §6(y) of the Participation Requirements.
questions.missing: Creatives API or PA-API credentials, which would supply compliant, current pricing.
questions.matters: A buying guide without prices is a real limitation for the reader.
questions.howToFind: Apply for PA-API access once the account has qualifying sales. Then prices can come from the API and stay accurate automatically.

questions.question: Can we show product images?
questions.answer: Not lawfully with what we have. Program Content cannot be copied or hot-linked outside approved tooling, and substituting a different appliance's photo would misrepresent the item.
questions.have: The constraint, quoted in the policy register.
questions.missing: Creatives API access, or manufacturer-supplied press assets with written permission.
questions.matters: Images are the single biggest lever on whether a product page converts.
questions.howToFind: PA-API/Creatives access is the correct route. Press kits are a fallback but add a per-brand permission burden.

questions.question: What disclosure is required, in what words, and where?
questions.answer: "As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases." — under the masthead on every page and repeated in the footer, plus a plain-language sponsored note on every outbound link.
questions.have: Operating Agreement §5 for the exact sentence; FTC Disclosures 101 for placement.
questions.missing: Nothing. Both requirements are explicit and quoted.
questions.matters: Violating §5 is a material breach, and a buried disclosure fails the FTC test.
questions.howToFind: Settled. The build now fails if either placement disappears.

questions.question: May we quote star ratings and review counts seen on the listing?
questions.answer: No. §6(t) forbids it without Creatives or PA-API.
questions.have: The clause, quoted verbatim.
questions.missing: API access to obtain ratings legitimately.
questions.matters: Ratings are the most tempting shortcut on an affiliate page, and the most commonly violated.
questions.howToFind: PA-API. Until then, the fields stay visibly withheld rather than quietly blank.

questions.question: Can the site run paid search ads?
questions.answer: Only narrowly. No bidding on Amazon marks or misspellings, and paid results must send users to this site, not to Amazon.
questions.have: §6(f) and the Prohibited Paid Search Placement definition.
questions.missing: Whether any ad budget exists at all.
questions.matters: An Amazon-branded ad campaign is a fast route to termination.
questions.howToFind: If ads are ever considered, read the Prohibited Paid Search Placement definition in the Commission Income Statement first.

questions.question: Is anything being measured right now?
questions.answer: No. The five events are defined and the client is written, but no collector is deployed, so the client is switched off.
questions.have: Event definitions and a self-hosted worker in _worker/.
questions.missing: A deployed endpoint, and a source of truth for orders — which can only be Associates reports.
questions.matters: The brief requires click and conversion measurement before content. Clicks can be counted; orders cannot be invented.
questions.howToFind: Deploy the worker and set the endpoint, then rebuild. Orders come from the Associates report, entered by hand into the ledger with a date.

questions.question: What belongs in the campaign ledger?
questions.answer: Only rows with a timestamp, source, channel, eligible sessions, clicks and reported orders from an authorized first-party report.
questions.have: A defined schema and an intentionally empty table.
questions.missing: Any actual report.
questions.matters: An empty honest ledger is useful. A ledger with placeholder numbers is a liability.
questions.howToFind: After the first tracked week, export the Associates report and add one row per channel, citing the report date.

questions.question: Will this site be indexed, and where?
questions.answer: GitHub Pages at /WinA/ is indexable, with a sitemap, feed, robots file and canonical URLs.
questions.have: A sitemap covering every public page, an RSS feed, and per-page canonical tags.
questions.missing: Search Console verification, so nobody can see whether indexing happened.
questions.matters: One site indexed well beats five competing with each other.
questions.howToFind: Replace the placeholder verification token, then submit sitemap.xml and check Coverage weekly until pages are indexed.

questions.question: Is a project subpath the right home for this?
questions.answer: It works, but a custom domain would be better for brand and for cookie scope.
questions.have: A working build at a /WinA/ subpath with all links correctly prefixed.
questions.missing: A domain name, and access to DNS.
questions.matters: A reader deciding whether to trust a buying guide reads the URL. A subpath reads as a side project.
questions.howToFind: Buy a domain, add a CNAME, enable HTTPS in Pages settings, then change baseurl in one place and rebuild.

questions.question: What is this publication called, and who is it for?
questions.answer: Working name 'Counter Space', for people deciding what earns counter space. Chosen for this build; not a permanent commitment.
questions.have: A name, voice, type system and colour palette applied consistently.
questions.missing: Confirmation that the requester wants this name and audience.
questions.matters: Every editorial choice flows from the audience. Renaming later means rewriting the voice.
questions.howToFind: Decision. Check the name is not already an active trademark in the same category before committing.

questions.question: Should there be an author identity?
questions.answer: Yes, eventually. Search quality guidance and reader trust both reward a real, attributable author.
questions.have: An editorial standards page describing method and constraints.
questions.missing: A named person, a bio, and any credentialed expertise to describe.
questions.matters: An unattributed review site reads as generated. That is exactly the failure mode the brief rejects.
questions.howToFind: Decide who is accountable for the content. A byline requires a real person willing to be named.

questions.question: Is there any traffic source at all beyond organic search?
questions.answer: None configured. No social presence, no email list, no referrals.
questions.have: An inert capture form and a feed.
questions.missing: An email service provider, and any distribution channel.
questions.matters: Organic search takes months. A site with no other channel is betting everything on one that has not started yet.
questions.howToFind: Pick one channel and commit, or accept a slow burn. Decide before spending effort on capture UI.

questions.question: Do the submitted short links actually reach the product pages, for a real visitor, right now?
questions.answer: Unresolved. Re-opening four of the five on 2026-11-20 returned the amazon.com home page; one returned a fetch error; an earlier attempt the same day returned the product page for the first link. The behaviour is not reproducible on command, so it cannot be recorded as either working or broken.
questions.have: The destination recorded by four separate sessions on 2026-11-20 (all five product pages, matching titles), plus this session's differing observations with their dates, and the listing pages re-read directly by ASIN.
questions.missing: A test from a device with a normal browser and cookies, which is the only environment that answers what a reader will see; and, for attribution, the matching entry in the Associates click report.
questions.matters: If a link dumps a reader on the storefront, the click is wasted and no commission is earned even when the enrolment is fine. It also decides whether the short links should ever be circulated outside the site.
questions.howToFind: Open each short link on a phone on cellular (not Wi-Fi, not a desktop browser), and note where it lands. Then click one tagged link from the site and check the Associates click report within 48 hours. This is Q-03, and it is the only remaining check that needs a human.

questions.question: Is commissioned illustration the right visual language, or should the site wait for licensed product images?
questions.answer: Decided for now, and reversible. The site publishes four original illustrations, each captioned as artwork rather than a product image, because the reader-facing page needs something to look at and Program Content cannot be stored or hot-linked. The gate enforces the rule that makes this honest: no Amazon asset, no stock appliance photo, alt text on every image, and nothing loaded from another host.
questions.have: The imagery clauses of the Operating Agreement and Program Policies as the register quotes them, the artwork itself, the build gate that classifies every image tag on every page, and FLG-038 recording the open question.
questions.missing: The owner's preference for how the brand should look, and Product Advertising API approval, which is the only route to real product imagery that the programme licenses.
questions.matters: A shop with no pictures asks readers to decide on text alone; a shop with borrowed or substituted pictures asks them to trust a claim about a product nobody here has photographed. The illustration route is the only option that is neither.
questions.howToFind: Owner: approve or reject on the suggestions page (SUG-27 is the API request that would end the trade-off). No research closes this one; it is a decision with a credential attached.

questions.question: Does the three-question chooser get more people to click a product link than the card grid does?
questions.answer: Unknown, and not guessable from here. The finder is built so the question can be answered: every one of its anchors carries data-slot="finder", while cards carry data-slot="card", hero carries data-slot="hero" and the register's citation links are declared non-affiliate. One event per outbound click separates them without any new instrumentation.
questions.have: The defined click event, the slot attributes already on every anchor, and the collector written but not deployed.
questions.missing: A deployed endpoint on a host the owner controls, the client flag turned on, and a few hundred sessions of traffic to compare slots. Nothing else about the finder can be tuned honestly before that exists.
questions.matters: It decides whether the chooser earns its place on the front page or gets demoted to the category hubs, and whether the next editorial cycle buys a quiz or buys articles.
questions.howToFind: Deploy _worker/collector.js (or scripts/analytics-server.mjs) behind the owner's domain, set site.analyticsEndpoint in data/products.json, and read the outbound_click counts grouped by slot after 500 sessions.
questions.sourceLabel: The collector written for this repository

questions.question: Which guide earns arrivals, and which one should the next topic be modelled on?
questions.answer: Not answerable yet. Every guide title on this site — including the two added on 2026-11-20 — is an editorial hypothesis chosen for the decision it clarifies, not for a measured query. The sitemap, feed and canonical set are in place for a search engine to read, and nothing has come back to rank them against.
questions.have: The published guide set, each in the sitemap and the feed on the day it ships, and a topics register that labels every roadmap title as a hypothesis.
questions.missing: Search Console verification (FLG-009), then two to four weeks of query data.
questions.matters: Without it, the seventh guide is as much a guess as the first. With it, the next topic comes from what people actually searched for, which is the only input that should reorder the roadmap.
questions.howToFind: Verify the domain in Search Console, submit the sitemap, and re-read the query report after two weeks. scripts/next-topics.mjs refuses to invent a ranking without an export, so it will say what it needs.

questions.question: The Emeril brand page publishes 120 volts. Does that settle the wattage row?
questions.answer: No. Voltage and power draw are different numbers, and converting one to the other needs a current figure nobody publishes for this model. The Wattage row therefore stays blank and marked unverified, while a new row states exactly what the brand does publish: "120 V; no wattage published on the brand page".
questions.have: The brand page's specification block as read on 2026-11-20, which lists 120 volts and no wattage, and the register's rule that a blank is published as a blank.
questions.missing: A published wattage from the brand or the listing. The product manual is linked from the brand page and may carry it; that is a five-minute check for the next data pass and it was not performed here.
questions.matters: Wattage is the number people compare when they worry about running a second oven on the same circuit. A guessed one would be the most consequential wrong figure on the page.
questions.howToFind: Read the linked installation manual for the model, or ask the brand. Until then the row stays blank, and the comparison table shows 'unverified' rather than an estimate.
